sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme; Institute for Social Research

sources.title: Karakalpakstan Agriculture Risk Profile for Climate Resilience Capacity Development
sources.temporal_coverage: Four-district climate-resilience risk profile published March 2025; assessment period not specified in the publisher summary.
sources.methodology: GGGI risk profile summarizes climate-resilience factors and vulnerability findings for four target districts in Karakalpakstan.
sources.limitations: Only the substantive publisher summary was accessible; it omits sample design, indicator construction, and district-specific breakdowns.

sources.title: Water and conflict in Central Asia
geographic_coverage: Amu Darya and Syr Darya basins
sources.temporal_coverage: Review published in 2025; assesses regional water/conflict evidence, including 1990-2024 and future prospects.
sources.methodology: Twelve-page research synthesis compares six water-scarcity metrics and reviews regional climate, water, and conflict evidence.
sources.limitations: Conflict evidence is regional, not Uzbekistan-specific; scarcity-conflict causality is debated.

sources.title: UNDP in Uzbekistan and Uzhydromet sum up the results of joint activities on developing climate resilience of farming communities in Karakalpakstan
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme; Center of Hydrometeorological Service of Uzbekistan (Uzhydromet)
sources.temporal_coverage: Adaptation Fund project implemented 2014-November 30, 2021; closeout results announced November 2021.
sources.methodology: UNDP-Uzhydromet project-closeout announcement reports equipment, service reach, and uptake figures presented at the final coordination meeting.
sources.limitations: This is a project announcement, not an independent evaluation; beneficiary counts may overlap and the page provides no comparison group or measured impact estimates.

sources.title: From local knowledge to local action: Communities shape restoration in three regions of Uzbekistan
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
geographic_coverage: Lower Amu Darya State Biosphere Reserve
sources.temporal_coverage: FAO-reported field visits and community workshops, including June 2026 consultations.
sources.methodology: FAO account summarizes field assessments, June 2026 workshops, participant proposals, and visits to candidate restoration sites under FOLUR-Uzbekistan.
sources.limitations: The page reports consultation findings and proposals, not a sampled vulnerability study, implemented restoration outcomes, or an independent evaluation.

claims.locator: Publisher report page, opening summary, paragraphs on water supply and four target districts.
claims.paraphrase: GGGI identifies restricted and declining drinking-water supply, associated with upstream diversion and long-term climate change, as a leading environmental danger for Karakalpakstan's four target districts: Bozataw, Chimbay, Karauzyak, and Kegeyli.
claims.limitations: The publisher summary does not show district-specific measurements or separate climate effects from upstream diversion.

claims.locator: Publisher report page, key conclusions, poverty and adaptive-capacity bullet.
claims.paraphrase: The profile reports that 76% of residents in the four target districts live below the poverty line, including 84% of young women and 86% of dehkans, and says this limits climate adaptive capacity.
claims.limitations: Rates are reported for the profile's target area; the publisher excerpt omits the sample, calculation method, and district breakdown.

claims.locator: Publisher report page, key conclusions, finance, training, and farm-strategy bullets.
claims.paraphrase: GGGI reports prohibitively high formal-finance rates, only 2% of respondents obtaining farm-management skills through formal training, and more than half of dehkan and homestead landowner groups lacking climate strategies.
claims.limitations: The report summary provides no subgroup or district breakdown and does not explain how capacity indicators were measured.

claims.locator: PDF p. 3 (printed p. 4), section 'Estimating the water shortage in Central Asia'; PDF p. 11, endnote vii.
claims.paraphrase: Across six metrics, NUPI ranks Uzbekistan as most water-insufficient in Central Asia; 9 of 13 provinces have high water stress, including four extremely high.
geographies: 13 provinces (province names not given in the cited text)
claims.limitations: The text names no provinces; this is a secondary synthesis.

claims.paraphrase: NUPI warns glacier-driven runoff shifts could intensify summer water tensions because Uzbekistan depends on summer irrigation flows; weak regional cooperation may threaten stability.
claims.scenario: No named emissions scenario is specified; this conditional future runoff shift is linked to warming and glacier melt.
geographies: Amu Darya and Syr Darya basins
claims.limitations: This conditional regional projection does not forecast conflict inside Uzbekistan or attribute past violence to climate.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Warming-related runoff shifts may intensify summer-water tensions, threatening regional stability without effective cooperation.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 9), 'Future prospects', paragraphs on seasonal runoff and regional cooperation.

claims.locator: Publisher page, paragraphs beginning 'During the event...' and 'Automation of the observations network...'.
claims.paraphrase: At project closeout, UNDP reported 10 automated meteorological stations and two equipped hydrological posts in Karakalpakstan, supporting drought early warnings with six-to-eight months' lead time for the lower Amu Darya.
claims.limitations: The closeout announcement reports installed capacity and forecast lead time, not independent forecast accuracy or verified use in crop decisions.

claims.locator: Publisher page, paragraphs beginning 'With the assistance of the project...' and '21,200 farmers...'.
claims.paraphrase: Three project advisory centers in Nukus and Kegeyli district served 21,200 farmers and household-land owners, including more than 6,000 women, according to UNDP's 2021 closeout account.
institutions: Tashkent State Agrarian University Nukus branch
claims.limitations: The announcement reports service reach without a unique-beneficiary method, usage frequency, or comparison group.

claims.locator: Publisher page, paragraphs beginning 'So about 41,200 people...' and 'As a result of project activities...'.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reports that 41,200 people applied resource-saving climate-resilient agriculture and 43,750 farmers used water-saving practices such as laser leveling and drip irrigation in Karakalpakstan.
claims.limitations: The beneficiary counts may overlap; the announcement gives no measured yield or water-savings estimate and is not an independent evaluation.

claims.locator: Publisher page, section 'Karakalpakstan: Water as the starting point', paragraphs on community-identified pressures.
claims.paraphrase: Participants near the Lower Amu Darya State Biosphere Reserve and Baday-Tugay connected land degradation with insufficient irrigation and drinking water, limited employment, and high agricultural costs; they identified reliable water as essential for restoration.
geographies: Lower Amu Darya State Biosphere Reserve
claims.limitations: These are participant-reported priorities from workshops and field visits, not quantified local indicators or causal estimates.

claims.locator: Publisher page, opening methods paragraphs and 'Restoration designed with and for communities'.
claims.paraphrase: Under FOLUR-Uzbekistan, farmers, pastoralists, women, protected-area staff, communities, and authorities reviewed restoration proposals, identified priority sites, and discussed implementation and maintenance roles across three regions, including Karakalpakstan.
institutions: National Committee on Ecology and Climate Change
claims.limitations: The article documents consultation activity; technical plans, confirmed sites, implementation, and benefits remained future steps.

claims.locator: Publisher page, 'Karakalpakstan: Water as the starting point', paragraphs on restoration proposals and community participation.
claims.paraphrase: Karakalpakstan participants supported restoring degraded Tugay forests near Baday-Tugay with native riparian species; FAO reports that water access and livelihood pressures will affect sustained community participation.
geographies: Lower Amu Darya State Biosphere Reserve
claims.limitations: The article describes a proposed restoration approach and conditions for future maintenance, not completed work or demonstrated resilience gains.

search_audit.query: Uzbekistan Karakalpakstan climate vulnerability drought water scarcity district report 2025 GGGI UNDP
search_audit.outcome: GGGI's four-target-district publisher summary provides named-district evidence. An additional publicly hosted Atlas was excluded because it is marked for internal use only.

search_audit.query: Uzbekistan climate change water scarcity conflict interstate tensions report source-stated climate Central Asia
search_audit.outcome: Found a regional research synthesis that explicitly describes conditional warming/runoff timing pathways to transboundary water tensions, with weak cooperation as a mediator; it does not attribute past violent events to climate change or identify Uzbekistan-specific violence.

search_audit.query: Karakalpakstan 2022 unrest climate water scarcity climate adaptation agriculture disruption; Uzbekistan conflict insecurity displacement constrains adaptation
search_audit.outcome: No substantive source located showing that conflict, insecurity, or displacement prevented a named Uzbek climate-adaptation activity or constrained its delivery. Search results on 2022 Karakalpakstan protests describe constitutional amendments as the trigger, not climate or adaptation access; that event is not linked to the climate claims here.

search_audit.query: Uzbekistan Karakalpakstan climate resilience adaptation project evaluation community UNDP FAO
search_audit.outcome: Found UNDP-Uzhydromet closeout-reported early-warning, farmer-service, and practice-uptake outputs, plus FAO-reported 2026 community consultation and restoration proposals. The GGGI full PDF and a UNDP final project review linked on a separate project page were not accessible; neither is used for claims.

gaps: No country-specific primary evidence was found that climate change caused violent conflict in Uzbekistan; NUPI's source-stated tension pathway is conditional and regional.

No evidence was located linking FCV events to blocked adaptation access, interruption of a named project, or reduced resilience delivery; the June 2022 protest trigger was constitutional, not climate-related.

Detailed methods and district-level figures for GGGI's four-district risk profile remain unavailable because the full report PDF could not be read; the Atlas was excluded because it is marked for internal use only.

The 2021 UNDP project counts are closeout-reported reach and practices, not independently measured climate-resilience impacts; the FAO 2026 account describes consultations and proposed restoration rather than completed outcomes.
